newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE's first equity fund attracts 250 mln dirhams.
newsitem.headline: UAE's first equity fund attracts 250 mln dirhams.

text.p: Subscription to the United Arab Emirates first equity fund has far exceeded expectations, attracting 250 million dirhams compared to the 30 million fund managers expected to raise, Emirates Bank International said.

"Initially we had expected around 30 million dirhams, but we clicked something in the market we did not expect. We were a little taken by surprise," EBI chief executive Anis al-Jallaf told a news conference late on Sunday.
He said that until late Sunday, when subscription at par of 100 dirhams a unit closed, the bank had received subscriptions for more than 250 million dirhams worth of units.

"We still see more subscriptions coming in," Jallaf said of the Emirates Equity Fund which will invest in the most active of the 30-odd companies traded regularly on the market, which EBI says is capitalised at 67 billion dirhams.
In the past year the market has risen by some 30 percent.

Jallaf said foreigners, including British and American institutions and individuals, had subscribed for more than the 20 percent ceiling allowed by the Central Bank in the open-ended fund. "Non-UAE nationals subscribed for about 23 percent," he said, adding that units would be allotted on a pro-rata basis.
Most foreigners applied for the maximum of 500,000 dirhams worth of units set for non-UAE nationals.

But Jallaf said EBI was still trying to get Central Bank approval for a higher foreign investment ceiling, possibly 49 percent. "We have gone back to the Central Bank to see if they can ease the restriction a little," he said.
About 75 percent of the UAE's population of 2.4 million people are foreigners, who have so far been excluded from the market, which is currently informal.
Jallaf expected other banks to set up similar funds to take advantage of the seven to nine initial public offerings he expects in the next 12 months.
